findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

The attestation shows the exact proof-plan argv failing with exit 1, no signal and no timeout. The expected-failure literal 'Required-result refusal must name the exact assertion' appears in the full, untruncated stdout. The failure comes from expectNamedRequiredRecovery after the real `safeword proof observe-bounded-delivery` CLI ran against a disposable committed full-source candidate. The CLI returned a refusal ('Fixed runner failed (exit 1, signal null); repair the lane and rerun') that does not name the controlled required assertion. That is the intended missing behavior at the actor boundary. It is not a syntax, import, fixture, configuration or infrastructure failure: earlier assertions on exit code 2, status 'refused' and execution-only authority passed before this message check. The proof exercises the scenario's When (a maintainer observation request through the Safeword CLI) and checks its Then (no successful observation, plus the result naming the assertion and a rerun action). I cannot recompute the source fingerprint from this packet, so I accept the fingerprint as bound to the supplied targets. There are no blocking errors, but there are discrimination and coverage warnings below.

Only the 'absent' outline row has RED evidence. The loop in bounded-observation-failures.node.ts stops at the first failing example, so the 'skipped' and 'failed' rows have never been seen failing for the right reason. The supporting note admits this. The rows share the same command and targets, as the Execution Plan allows, but RED credit for 'skipped' and 'failed' is unproven. A 'skipped' candidate could still fail for a wrong reason, for example a registration-check failure, or pass vacuously once 'absent' turns GREEN. Fix: make each outcome its own node:test subtest, or run with per-row isolation, so each row's failure is observed independently.

The naming check is weakly discriminating. It only tests `message.includes(controlledAssertion.fullName)`. An implementation that adds every required assertion name to any runner-failure refusal would pass all three rows without identifying which assertion lacked a passing result or what that result was (absent, skipped or failed). Fix: also assert that a different required assertion which still passes, for example 'planning scope review contract makes persona outcomes and epistemic status Product approval questions', is not named as the problem. Where the result data exposes it, also assert the outcome category for each row.

The 'absent' control renames the test declaration. That also makes the registration check (bdd-proof-tags.test.ts) fail, so the runner exits nonzero for reasons beyond the missing result. This mixes in the separate 'failed runner cannot hide behind passing assertions' scenario. The note acknowledges this, and requiring the named assertion even on a nonzero runner exit is a reasonable target. Still, the GREEN implementation must grade the retained report on runner failure without letting the runner-failure message stand in for the required-result refusal.

The attested parent Node is v24.3.0, while the plan pins v24.18.1, and expectResolvedTools on the success path asserts v24.18.1. This doesn't affect this refusal-path RED, because the observer reached the runner. It may matter for later success-path proofs on this host.

The test's own timeout is 900_000 ms, but the attestation timeout is 600_000 ms. Three candidates at about 90 s each fit inside both, but the mismatch could produce a misleading timeout if per-row runtime grows.
